description.value: The study examined behavioral and neural responses associated with cognitive reappraisal in generalized social anxiety disorder compared with healthy controls across three socio-emotional fMRI tasks.

spans.text: The goal of the present study was to examine behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses in patients with SAD compared to healthy controls (HC) when reappraising socio-emotional stimuli.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study comparing 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls during three tasks, each containing React and Reappraise conditions, with analyses of BOLD magnitude and early versus late temporal responses.

spans.text: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) of blood oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) signal, we examined reappraisal-related behavioral and neural responses in 27 participants with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls (HC) during three socio-emotional tasks: (1) looming harsh faces (Faces); (2) videotaped actors delivering social criticism (Criticism); and (3) written autobiographical negative self-beliefs (Beliefs).
To assess social anxiety symptom severity, participants completed the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale-Self-Report (LSAS-SR) [ ].

description.value: This questionnaire assesses both fear and behavioral avoidance of social situations.

Faces task

task_description.value: Participants viewed looming harsh faces and either reacted normally or reappraised their emotional response.

spans.text: This task consisted of 24 trials during which the participants viewed color photos of faces displaying Ekman facial action coded anger and contempt facial expressions [ ].
All tasks were programmed in Eprime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc.).

instructions.value: React normally or try to down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

spans.text: During the ‘Reappraise’ condition, participants were instructed to try and down regulate negative emotion reactions by actively reinterpreting the meaning of the emotion inducing stimulus.

stimuli.value: Color photos of faces displaying anger and contempt facial expressions, appearing to move closer to simulate looming.

spans.text: Each trial consisted of a cue (Look or Reframe) lasting 1.5 s, a single harsh facial stimulus presented in color and appearing to move closer to the participant to simulate looming

task_performance_measures.value: negative emotion rating from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much)

spans.text: After each trial, participants provided a negative emotion rating using a button response pad positioned in the participant’s right hand inside the magnet by responding to ‘How negative do you feel?’ (1 = not at all to 5 = very much).
Criticism task

task_description.value: Participants viewed videotaped actors delivering social criticism and either reacted or reframed their response; only criticism evaluation periods were analyzed.

spans.text: The task consisted of videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise and harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions
All tasks were programmed in Eprime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc.).

instructions.value: React to social criticism or reappraise the emotion by thinking that the statement is not always true or is only a thought, not a fact.

spans.text: Participants were told to react to the social criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise their emotion, for example by thinking: ‘this is not always true’, or ‘this is only a thought, not a fact’.

stimuli.value: Videotaped actors delivering social criticism and praise with harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions.

spans.text: The task consisted of videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise and harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions
After each video clip, participants were cued to rate their current negative emotion (3 s).
Beliefs task

task_description.value: Participants reacted to or reframed autobiographical social anxiety-related negative self-beliefs embedded in written situations.

spans.text: At the scanner, the participants were asked to either React to the negative self-beliefs, or to Reframe their reaction.
All tasks were programmed in Eprime (Psychology Software Tools, Inc.).

instructions.value: React to negative self-beliefs or reappraise by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenges the thoughts.

spans.text: Participants were trained prior to scanning to react to the NSBs by reflecting on how the NSB represents something that is true about themselves, or to reappraise their reaction by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenges the thoughts

stimuli.value: Written autobiographical social anxiety situations and participant-generated negative self-beliefs.

spans.text: four participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situations that were characterized by social anxiety, humiliation, and/or embarrassment

Each situation consisted of an instruction to react/reframe (1.5 s), 16 sentences (3 s each,) in white font against a black background describing the situation, 10 NSBs (9 s each) embedded in the unfolding story in uppercase letters that flashed nine times (850 ms on + 150 ms off), and a negative emotion rating after each NSB (3 s).
